dedupe_keys.name: southern african power pool sapp interconnector transfer limits demand and supply balance and market reports

description: The Southern African Power Pool was created in August 1995 at the SADC summit in Kempton Park, when SADC member governments (excluding Mauritius) signed an inter-governmental memorandum to pool electricity across the region; the revised memorandum was signed on 23 February 2006. Its website publishes technical and market information for the interconnected southern African grid. Coverage: SADC member utilities; a demand and supply table lists, for each country utility (Angola RNT, Botswana BPC, DRC SNEL, Eskom, ZESCO, ZESA and others), installed and operating capacity, peak demand, reserves and the resulting excess or shortfall (67,266 MW installed and 50,865 MW peak demand in the table read); a transfer limits table gives each interconnector with voltage, number of lines, thermal, voltage and stability limits and the applicable transfer limit; monthly market performance reports (for example August 2026: 191.2 GWh traded, a third of matched bids not traded because of central corridor congestion); plus annual and monthly reports, planned outages, a grid map, statistics, the pool plan and a draft master plan. Format and access: HTML tables and PDF reports (over 130 market report PDFs linked), free on sapp.co.zw; some areas need a member login. Licence: not stated on the pages read. Caveats: the demand and supply table carries no date and uses older utility names, so it may be out of date; the statistics and grid map pages rendered no content without scripts. Simulation uses: interconnector limits and national capacity balances for regional power flow, cross-border trade and supply adequacy models. Related records: Eskom's data portal (data-eskom-data-portal) holds South African system data behind the largest member.
